feedback: If the 'range = two extremes' sentence is picked: 'Range is one number — the difference. The two end values are the extremes, a different thing.'
If a patternless scatter is sorted as 'positive' or 'negative': 'No clear trend means no correlation — correlation is about the direction of a trend.'
If the mode is matched to the 'average' slot: 'The most frequent value is the mode; the mean is the add-and-divide typical value — different words.'
activities.intendedInsight: Correct use can be probed by matching and categorising against a data context — this surfaces swaps without asking the child to recite a definition.
learnerActions: On a given ordered data set, match each word — mean, median, mode, range — to the value it names.
Sort a set of scatter graphs into positive / negative / no correlation.
Choose which sentence uses 'range' correctly, where a distractor names the two extreme values ('0 and 8') instead of their difference (8).
Judge statements as 'uses the word correctly' or 'incorrectly' (e.g. 'the median is the middle of the unordered list', 'the mode is the average').
activities.title: Match and sort: check correct use, not definitions

feedback: Character confirms correct use: 'Yes — the mode is the most common score, and you named it right.'
Character queries a misuse: 'You called the most common value the average — is that the mode or the mean?'
activities.intendedInsight: Talking through a data story and being gently pressed on word choice surfaces swaps in the moment and rehearses precise use.
learnerActions: Take on a 'data detective' role: a character presents a data story and asks the child to describe it.
Describe the data aloud, choosing the right statistical words.
Respond when the character echoes back correct usage or queries a misuse — e.g. 'You said the range is 0 and 8 — can a range be two numbers?'
activities.title: Data detective: catch the swap in conversation
